To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the structural and electrochemical study on Li intercalation into the WO 3.H 2 O crystal structure shows that the Li intercalation is reversible up to 0.35 Li/WO 3.

The intercalation of lithium into WO 3 H 2 O leads to four different phases, called α, β, γ and δ, and the modification of the lattice parameter b is a reliable way to characterize the structural changes induced during the intercalation.
Li intercalation of the infrared reflectance plastic material o -Li x (WO 3 ·H2O) is possible, but that the intercalated phases are not reversible.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of new materials and devices based on the insertion of ions in the interlayer of layered materials, and with the understanding of the structural modifications induced by the insertion/deinsertion of the ions.
the development of new electrochromic materials, and the understanding of the electrochemical behavior of such materials.
the development of a new class of materials, which can be reversibly modulated between two different states of reflectance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the α phase is stable and reversible, whereas the β, γ and especially the δ phase are not.
Li intercalation in o -WO 3 ·H2O leads to a progressive increase in the symmetry of the crystal structure.
the α 2 phase ( x =0.30) is the most stable phase and the most appropriate for building a variable infrared reflectance modulator.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the α 1 phase is the best candidate for the realization of a reversible variable infrared reflectance modulator.
the Li intercalated phase of the infrared modulating compound L i x W O 3 ·H2O exhibits a structural behavior similar to that of the intercalation of Li in the Li x W O 2 compound.
the Li intercalation of the WO 3 -based infrared modulating compound o -Li x (WO 3 ·H2O) leads to an increasing symmetry of the crystal structure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Li intercalation in the WO 3 lattice is accompanied by a reversible modification in the distance separating the tungsten layers.
the α 2 phase is the best phase to be used for the fabrication of the plastic infrared reflectance modulator.
the α 2 subphase is the most stable phase for Li intercalation and that it is possible to cycle reversibly between α 2 and α 0 phases without any major degradation of structure.
